name: Gilyak
catalog_quote: In WSN, stress is fixed on the first syllable in a polysyllabic stem. Phonetic correlates of stress are the assignment of high pitch in the citation form and for some speakers palatalization of the consonant before front vowels /i, e/

sources.quote: Instrumental (oscillographic, LGU experimental phonetics lab) study of Amur-dialect speakers. It does not state the syllable position of word stress. Its finding is at the word-complex level: in object+verb 'incorporative' complexes the verb loses intensity and its vowel shortens ~1.5x while the preceding object keeps full intensity (p.85), and in lyghi-n'yng-nivx 'salmon-catching man' there is a single amplitude peak on the first component (p.89) — i.e. one prominence, on the leftmost member of the complex. Consistent with Shiraishi's first-constituent primary stress in compounds/phrases, but
sources.locator: pp. 84-89 (issue PDF); speakers = five Amur-dialect Nivkh students (fn.5, p.84)
